Macrons

Consonantal i

SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Kitchen, meals & drinks · Body, health & movement

herbal tea noun

also infusion, mint tea, herb tea, tisane, decoction, chamomile tea, linden tea, home remedy

modern

M-O s.v. tea: herb tea

1īnfūsum: long i (Morgan–Owens infûsum, a Neo-Latin noun marked *). As in īnfundō, īnfūsus: in- is long before f.

īnfūsum1, īnfūsī n.

noun, second declension

herbal tea, infusion

With a genitive; also dēcoctum.

Other words

  • mentae īnfūsum — mint tea

    also used · modern · M-O s.v. tea: herb tea

  • dēcoctum, dēcoctī n. — decoction, the liquid so made

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Pliny; M-O s.v. tea: herb tea, decoctum with the genitive

  • īnfūsum flōrum tiliae — linden-blossom tea

    also used · our formation

    Our formation on M-O’s pattern. Pliny knows linden bark for swellings and wounds (NH 24.49), not the blossom tea.

Examples

  • Īnfūsum tibi chamaemēlī parābō.

    I’ll make you some chamomile tea.composed

  • Exspectā dum refrīgēscat; nimis calidum est.

    Wait for it to cool down; it’s too hot.composed

  • Hīc mentam et serpyllum legāmus, ut domī īnfūsum faciāmus.

    Let’s pick mint and wild thyme here, to make tea at home.composed

See also tea, sip, boil down, chamomile, mint, linden, honey, remedy, cold.

SourcesMorgan–Owens: Silva

Lewis & Short: infundo · Lewis & Short: refrigesco

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. tea: herb tea. John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency has no entry for herb tea.

Pliny (NH 24.49) checked against the Perseus Latin texts.

The example sentences marked “composed” are ours.
